chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Do you think that if a man were to enter his house and lock his door, anything would fall upon him from the sky?

key_terms.أَ رَأَيْتَ: Rhetorical phrase meaning 'Do you see/think?' — used to make the listener reflect critically
key_terms.السَّمَاء: The sky/heaven — here contrasted with active effort; sustenance does not fall from the sky without one going out to earn it

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the necessity of seeking one's livelihood?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) poses a rhetorical question to underscore the necessity of going out and actively seeking one's livelihood. The Imam challenges the notion that sustenance descends passively without effort, implying that one must go out into the world and engage in work and trade. This teaching was delivered in the context of urging believers not to be passive or withdraw from the marketplace but to take initiative in earning their living.
